text:
Alex: quick heads-up — seen an odd KV residency pattern on qwen-32b-prod. long-chat sessions climb in a staircase: memory jumps ~+4GB each ~2k tokens instead of steady growth.
Sofia: yup, telemetry showed plateaus then jumps. looks aligned with batching boundaries and rope scaling. grabbing traces now. :thinking_face:
Alex: is this the same as the old 'ghost pages' thing? or something new with MQA/GQA?
Jamal: repro'd locally on cpu-gpu-edge. simple warmup then 3 concurrent long requests replicates it. will paste commands.
Jamal: ```
# repro (short)
for i in 1 2 3; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \n    -d '{"model":"qwen-32b","input":"repeat: long_context","max_tokens":22000}' &
done
wait
```
Sofia: attached pprof snapshot (excerpt):
```
(pprof) top
40.2%  runtime/kv::alloc_slab
18.6%  runtime/kv::pin_pages
9.9%   runtime/kv::mark_resident
6.4%   kernels/mqa_fallback
4.3%   batcher::flush_on_boundary
```
Maya: interesting the kernel fallback shows up. my theory: when kernel selector chooses MQA-compatible kernels for slices of the sequence, the allocator uses larger page units to satisfy alignment -> those pages get pinned until a batch boundary triggers eviction, so residency steps when boundaries hit.
Alex: makes sense. which models? only Qwen or also Mistral/LLama?
Sofia: seen strongest on Qwen (gqa/mqa mixed runtime), mild on Mistral when rope scaling factor > 1.5, almost nothing on base Llama.
Jamal: raw numbers from one run: baseline mem 18.1GB -> after ~2k tokens 22.2GB -> after ~4.5k tokens 26.4GB -> final 34.1GB. each bump corresponds to a batcher flush in traces.
Maya: two-pronged mitigation I think: 1) avoid pinning entire page ranges on kernel fallback (adaptive pin granularity), 2) change batching heuristic to prefer keeping long-context streams on same batch slot so they don't cross boundaries randomly.
Sofia: also ran an experiment: enabling small-page mode for qwen model reduces jumps but increases kernel overhead ~+6% CPU. tradeoff.
Alex: can we add per-model slab_hint in model catalog so Qwen uses different allocation policy?
Maya: yes, we can add slab_hint + eviction_bias per-model. simple config toggle for Dedicated/Private.
Jamal: reproduced with a quick patch to runtime toggling small_page=true for qwen -> memory curve smooths, final mem ~27GB instead of 34GB. latency tail +1.8%.
Sofia: logs (snippet):
```
[trace] batcher: flush boundary idx=8 on seq_len=2048 -> evict candidate pages=512 pinned=128
[trace] kv: mark_resident page_idx=2047 size=64k slab_id=3 model=qwen-32b kernel=mqa_fallback
[warn] kv: eviction skipped due to cross-batch pin, reason=batch_cross_pin
```
Alex: curious if this interacts with rope scaling (positional growth). does moving rope scale change bump frequency?
Maya: yes, higher rope scaling moves batch alignment earlier -> more frequent smaller bumps. we saw shift when rope_scale increased from 1.0 -> 1.4.
Sofia: propose short action items:
- add deterministic repro to eng-runtime ci (Jamal)
- experiment with per-model slab_hint and small_page toggle (Maya + Sofia)
- telemetry check: add metric kv.bump_count and bump_size per model (Alex)
- longer-term: change kernel selector to avoid full-page pin on fallback (research/eng)

Jamal: created a local test branch and a ci job "kv-residency-staircase" that runs the loop for 10m, ping me if you want access.
ci-bot: CI run kv-residency-staircase #42 completed: baseline->peak delta = +16GB over 10m, regression confirmed on qwen-32b image. (link omitted) :boom:
Alex: OK let's triage: assign to eng-runtime and eng-ml inference. @Maya can you own the per-model slab_hint POC? @Jamal please add repro to the infra ci. @Sofia add kv.bump_count to console and a short dashboard.
Maya: assigned, will put up draft PR for slab_hint + small_page flag. ETA EOD tomorrow.
Sofia: I'll add the dashboard tiles and a quick regression alert (kv.bump_count > 3 in 5m).
Alex: thanks all — this one explains a bunch of weird long-chat OOMs we've been seeing in support tickets. tagging @oncall if it spikes.
Jamal: FYI I also tried with llama-70b-mqa emulation and didn't see the same amplitude, so it's model-kernel interaction not purely allocator bug.
Maya: good, helps narrow to kernel+alloc coupling.
Alex: cool, keep updates here. :thumbsup:
